did.abstract: The Glimpses of Brooklyn viewbooks are comprised of 25 black-and-white non-photographic prints of photographs depicting views of Brooklyn, circa 1890. The viewbooks were published by the Mercantile Illustrating Company in 1894.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: One viewbook was a gift of William Schroeder, M.D., date unknown. The source and date of acquisition of the second viewbook is unknown. The viewbooks were formally accessioned in 1986.

altformavail.head: Existence and Location of Copies
altformavail.p: Item level description and digital versions of images from the collection are available for searching via the image database in the library under the call number prefixes V1986.12 and V1986.13.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: These two copies of the same viewbook are housed in a single folder with no particular order.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: Viewbooks, also called souvenir albums or view albums, are books that contain commercially published groups of photographs depicting a place, activity, or event.

processinfo.p: This collection combines the accessions V1986.012 and V1986.013.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Other viewbooks for specific neighborhoods in Brooklyn (such as Coney Island and Flatbush) are also held at CBH.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Glimpses of Brooklyn viewbooks are comprised of 25 black-and-white non-photographic prints of photographs depicting views of Brooklyn, circa 1890. The viewbooks were published by the Mercantile Illustrating Company in 1894. Images of Prospect Park, the Brooklyn Bridge, Green-Wood Cemetery, and Brooklyn Heights are included and captions accompany each image. Each viewbook contains 23 pages, measuring 7.2 x 10.5. One of the original softcovers has been recovered with a hardcover library binding that is now brittle, while many of its pages have separated from its binding. The other viewbook retains its original softcover, but some of its pages were previously water damaged.
